outcome.reason: Accept for modest repository integration credit. The contributed work defines a finite-relation-to-list-CNF representation, establishes its evaluation semantics and complement correspondence, and connects assignment updates to the explicitly attributed upstream graph restriction lemma. This supplies a reusable compatibility result for the protocol-style evaluator, beyond merely reproducing the upstream statement. The underlying mathematics is elementary and known: setting a positive variable to true satisfies its incident clauses, leaving the remaining edge clauses unchanged. Neither that observation nor the retained upstream proof merits discovery credit. The evidence reports formal verification, but the mathematical scope is only positive two-literal graph CNFs; it supplies no complexity bound, arbitrary-CNF result, or resolution of P versus NP. The noncomputable conversion and locally reproduced evaluator definitions further limit practical significance. Treat the semantic bridge and its supporting lemmas as one small contribution, with honest upstream attribution and no separate merit for the reproduced material. No supplied prior or related record establishes that this integration was already credited.

The submission provides a formal integration bridge between a graph-theoretic restriction lemma (L_meta_253) and a specific list-based CNF evaluation protocol. While the core graph result is acknowledged as upstream work (lshhhhhhh), the contributor has implemented the semantic mapping (relationCNF) and proven the compatibility lemmas (relationCNF_semantics, relationCNF_complement, and complement_update) necessary to relate vertex deletion in a graph to assignment updates in the CNF representation. This is useful incremental formalization work that connects two different representations of the same problem. The work is modest in scope and does not claim to resolve the full P versus NP problem.
